title: Morning Edition
dek: Taiwan's unannounced naval exercises, Congo's Ebola emergency, Hera at its target, and the social meaning of awkwardness.

lead_story.headline: Taiwan reports large unannounced Chinese naval drills across the western Pacific
lead_story.summary: Taiwanese officials say more than 100 Chinese naval and coast-guard vessels participated in early-November exercises, including operations that appeared designed to restrict outside access. Beijing described carrier activity as routine and did not acknowledge a named exercise.
lead_story.why_it_matters: The scale and coordination raise questions about maritime access and crisis signaling ahead of the APEC summit, without establishing that an attack is imminent.

items.headline: Congo's Ebola outbreak passes 11,000 reported cases
items.summary: Congolese authorities report 11,042 cases and 5,387 deaths in the Bundibugyo outbreak. WHO's earlier November 3 situation report documented 10,668 cases, showing the outbreak's continuing growth amid conflict and difficult contact tracing.
items.why_it_matters: The public-health challenge is not only medical: access, trust and safe monitoring of exposed people are essential to containment.

items.headline: Iran says nuclear monitoring cannot resume under military threats
items.summary: Iran told the IAEA that restoring inspections is impossible while threats of new attacks continue. The agency says its access to damaged sites and verification of highly enriched uranium remain inadequate.
items.why_it_matters: An expanding information gap makes nuclear risk harder to assess independently, even as both sides dispute the conditions for inspections.

items.headline: Europe's Hera spacecraft begins close study of an asteroid NASA struck
items.summary: ESA's Hera mission has reached the Didymos-Dimorphos system and begun inspecting the aftermath of NASA's 2022 DART collision. Its instruments will investigate how the impact changed the moonlet and dispersed debris.
items.why_it_matters: The measurements can help turn one successful asteroid-deflection demonstration into a better-understood planetary-defense technique.

items.headline: Brazil's inflation stays above target despite a softer October reading
items.summary: Brazil's October annual inflation rate was 4.63%, up slightly from September but below economists' median forecast. The central bank continues to face high borrowing costs and pressure to reduce inflation.
items.why_it_matters: A modestly better monthly surprise does not erase the underlying policy tradeoff between prices, growth and debt costs.

items.headline: Older catch-up: an ancient Maya city emerges from Yucatán forest
items.summary: An archaeological team reported a previously undocumented Maya urban center called Minanbé, with monuments, palatial buildings and a pyramid. The site had remained difficult to access through dense vegetation.
items.why_it_matters: A major settlement hidden in plain sight is a reminder of how incomplete our maps of ancient population and infrastructure remain.

items.headline: Stratford's annual craft fair reaches its 25th year
items.summary: The Rotary Christmas Arts and Crafts Festival opens November 13 in Stratford, Ontario, with 89 vendors, model trains and children's activities. Proceeds support local community projects.
items.why_it_matters: A familiar annual fair offers a small view of how a town's volunteer organizations sustain local traditions.

items.headline: Awkwardness may be a shared social problem, not a personal defect
items.summary: Philosopher Alexandra Plakias argues that awkward moments expose clashes between social expectations and can suppress necessary conversations. The problem is not simply that some people lack social skill.
items.why_it_matters: Treating discomfort as a feature of social norms rather than an individual's failure can change when people decide to speak.

worth_your_time.headline: The cyberattack epidemic may be less straightforward than its headlines
worth_your_time.summary: A reported long read traces disruptive hacks involving refrigeration systems, cryptocurrency and false alerts. Experts distinguish real weaknesses in old connected devices from unproven claims that AI has already transformed every attack.
worth_your_time.why_it_matters: The article separates demonstrated technical risks from dramatic extrapolation and asks what durable digital infrastructure requires.

daily_wonder.title: The passenger pigeon, drawn before its disappearance
daily_wonder.caption: An Audubon image of a male and female passenger pigeon, reproduced as a lithograph. Once abundant across North America, the species became extinct in 1914; the plate preserves the appearance of a bird that no living person can now observe in the wild.
daily_wonder.alt: Historical color illustration of two passenger pigeons perched on branches, one bending toward the other.
daily_wonder.credit: John James Audubon (original painting); J. T. Bowen (lithograph); Wikimedia Commons reproduction
daily_wonder.rights: Public domain in the United States (published before 1931); Public Domain Mark 1.0

reflection.passage: The best way of avenging thyself is not to become like [the wrong-doer].
reflection.author: Marcus Aurelius
reflection.context: In this Stoic meditation, a response to wrongdoing is judged by the character it forms in the person responding, not by how closely it mirrors the original injury.
reflection.question: Which response preserves the standards you want to live by?
